reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While Plan B focuses solely on easy trail runs, Plan A incorporates strength training and tempo runs, which are crucial for developing speed and efficiency on trails. The inclusion of strength and mobility work in Plan A addresses injury prevention and builds a foundation for more intense training, while the tempo runs directly target improving speed at a sustainable effort level. Plan B's repetitive easy runs, while good for base building, lack the stimulus needed to drive significant improvements in speed.
